ruling.recommended_action: Issue a Ryde voucher of $3.62 to the rider (RD-2 mileage overcharge on the non-exempt off-route segment) and note the RD-1 finding on the driver's record.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a metered RydeTAXI journey whose optimal route was 16.5 km but 19.1 km was driven, +2.6 km (+16%) [F1], with one measured off-route segment 21:57–22:04 driving 4.13 km where the optimal route covers 1.77 km, adding 2.36 km and reaching up to 1304 m off route [F3]. That segment is an off-route segment under RD-1 which no exemption excuses, so RD-2 applies and the extra metered mileage on it is refundable [F3][RD-1][RD-2].

RD-5 fails: there is no in-app chat at all between rider and driver [F8], so no rider message sent before 21:57:35 agrees to the route or its scope. The only proffered agreement is the driver's post-trip statement "I went round it" [F9], and a driver's claim of agreement appearing only in his statement is not consent, nor can a message sent after the segment establish consent. The complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment means the segment counts [F8][F9][RD-5]. RD-3 likewise gives no relief: no rider-requested stop was named or measured in this segment, so nothing is exempt on that basis [F3][RD-3].

RD-4 also fails as a screen: the accident on Ayer Rajah Expressway was reported at 22:07 at 0 m from the optimal route, i.e. after the off-route segment began at 21:57 and near the trip's end [F3][F12], so it cannot supply the reasonable cause required for an exemption of that already-completed stretch; the speed-band records for Ayer Rajah Expressway and Central Expressway (band 4, 30–39 km/h) are not band 1 or 2 and in any case speed band alone does not exempt [F10][F11][RD-4]. The driver's "accident ... unavoidable" claim is therefore not corroborated against the replaced stretch [F9][RD-4].

Amount: the trip's per-km rate is the fare record's distance fare ÷ distance km = $26.93 ÷ 19.10 km = $1.4099/km [F7], and the fare record already bills excess distance of $3.62 on 2.57 km at that rate [F4]. The non-exempt segment's extra 2.36 km × $1.4099/km = $3.33; the trace's formula and the fare record's own excess basis (2.57 km × $1.4099 = $3.62) both cap what is refundable, so the refund is $3.62 [F3][F4][F7][RD-2]. The 0.1 min of meter waiting ($0.02) is meter waiting time under RD-3(c) and is not refunded [F5][RD-3]. RD-6 is not triggered: the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days, so no account flag is added [F15][RD-6].

No rider-named stop covers this stretch either [F3]. The 2.36 km extra is refundable under RD-2 [RD-1][RD-2][RD-3][RD-5].

events.body:
RIDER: You were charged for a detour on your RydeTAXI ride. We compared the route driven with the best route: the driver took an off-route stretch that added about 2.36 km beyond what the trip needed, and we found no valid reason for it. Because that stretch was metered, we're refunding the extra fare of $3.33 as a Ryde voucher, which will be applied to your account. Nothing else on your fare is being refunded, and your account hasn't been flagged — this was a one-off. If you see this again, report the trip in the app.

We compared the route you drove with the best route and found a stretch where you went off-route without a valid reason, adding about 2.36 km to the metered distance. The extra fare of $3.33 is being refunded to the rider as a Ryde voucher, and this breach is noted on your record. No action has been taken on your account beyond that note; repeated route issues could lead to a review. Stick to the suggested route unless the rider asks otherwise.
